observations.method: Compared 12 source descriptions with stored Items and selected awareness, opposed skill, spell restraint, advancement and wound-threshold paths; static inspection only.
observations.scope: Light Sleeper, Naive, Keen Intuition, Stubborn, Observant, Attention to Detail, Big Words, Questioning, Creative, Scholar, Weak Bones and Social Stigma.
observations.limitations: Questioning's helper requires a flag absent from the inspected opposed callers. Manual and partially implemented clauses, choices, stored results, restrictions, duplicate modifiers, XP, interruptions, actor types and concurrent use remain unverified. No Foundry session or automated tests were run.

observations.method: Compared 20 character traits with the available Core descriptions, stored configuration, skill and trait paths, and the language integration; static inspection only.
observations.scope: Direction Sense, Addictions, Aversion, Combat Paralysis, Common Sense, Disturbing Voice, Oblivious, First Impression, Attractive, Amnesia, Timid, Dampened Senses, Incompetent, Good with Animals, Brave, Preferred Enemy, Situational Awareness, Unremarkable, Illiterate and Ugly.
observations.limitations: The recorded clauses require individual manual adjudication and tracking, including choices, circumstances, test modifiers and expiry. Illiterate also has a language integration path whose behavior needs native verification. Existing actor values and other integrations may affect the outcome; inspect before applying adjustments. No Foundry session or automated tests were run.

observations.method: Compared 20 immunity, resistance, weakness and numeric-trait Items with the Core rules, stored type/value, actor aggregation, damage, condition, disease and resistance-test paths; static inspection only.
observations.scope: Six Immunities, four Resistances, six Weaknesses, Disease Resistance, Power Well, Natural Toughness and Resist Normal Weapons. The resolver now checks damage-type immunity per component; the alternate zero-HP wound trigger checks the prior HP.
observations.limitations: Non-damaging immunity effects, mixed damage, weakness post-mitigation order and penalties, source-backed X, edited or duplicate traits, legacy fields, old outcomes, immunity with Spell Absorption and both wound modes need live review. The six cleaned Weakness descriptions remain source-only. No Foundry session or automated tests were run.

observations.method: Compared 16 racial talents clause by clause against the supplied Core extracts, stored configuration, passive contributors, activation, Luck, damage, healing and expiry paths; static inspection only.
observations.scope: Blood of Aldmeris, Highborn, Child of the Sap, Histskin, Nature’s Blessing, Lionheart, Dragonskin, Red Diamond, Imperial Luck, Eye of Night, Sons of Skyrim, Wrothgarian, Malacath’s Fury, High Men, Adrenaline Burst and Ancestor’s Protection.
observations.limitations: Recognized Highborn, Dragonskin, Histskin, Malacath’s Fury and Ancestor’s Protection activations stop before cost or use. Recognized Adrenaline Rush is held only when enabled Adrenaline Burst applies. Passive contributions, older effects and pending outcomes need individual GM review; the modified power’s Fatigue alternative remains unresolved. No Foundry session or automated tests were run.

observations.method: Compared 14 additional Core combat talents and their stored configuration with attack, defense, reload, damage, movement and skill paths; static inspection only.
observations.scope: Rapid Reload, Unstoppable Might, Follow-up Strike, Mighty Cleave, Unrelenting, Back to Back, Teamwork, Unarmed Defender, Crackshot, Unarmed Prowess, Thunder Charge, Armored Agility, Skirmisher and Slash and Stash.
observations.limitations: Rapid Reload, Unstoppable Might special wield, Follow-up Strike, Mighty Cleave and Thunder Charge now require manual handling at the identified entry points. Crackshot no longer forces Agility; Armored Agility counts the selected-characteristic penalty only when actually applied. Old cards and prior partial writes remain unchanged. No Foundry session or automated tests were run.

observations.method: Reviewed the 51 unmatched Item identities, stored values, related Core evidence, inventory and item-use paths; static inspection only.
observations.scope: Fifteen gemstone variants, seven legacy rarity poisons, five seeded poison levels, nine toxins, eight raw materials, two tools, Skooma, a Great Welkynd Stone, Claws and two robes.
observations.limitations: Exact profiles and prices remain unresolved and are preserved. Poison/toxin application and old resistance cards are held for GM resolution because their prior separate writes could lose a hit or outcome. No Foundry session or automated tests were run.

observations.method: Compared 26 named Core feature entries, stored configuration and each described clause with the relevant initiative, combat, damage, activation and recovery paths; static inspection only.
observations.scope: 18 features previously lacked selected diagnostic traces; eight had earlier selected traces. Step Aside, Gladiator, Defender, Perfect Hit, Killing Blow and Combat Senses receive additional safeguards.
observations.limitations: Many clauses still require manual adjudication. The choice, roll, AP or SP, target, condition, expiry, permissions, interrupted writes and concurrent-client cases are not live verified. Earlier rolls, costs, free-defense markers and damage are not repaired. No Foundry session or automated tests were run.

observations.method: Compared selected Core character trait clauses on pages 55–57 with their stored fields, actor preparation, skill, wound, initiative, surprise, disease and condition paths; static inspection only.
observations.scope: Low Pain Tolerance, Pain Tolerant, Weak Immune System, Lingering Injury, Star Cursed, Blind, Threat Awareness, Bad Reflexes, Perfect Memory and Slippery.
observations.limitations: The selected trait entries contain a mixture of existing passive fields and clauses requiring manual resolution. Check each entry's instructions and inspect already-applied modifiers before adding another. Lingering Injury's one SP needs confirmation of how the source intends the maximum or current pool to change. Low Pain Tolerance and Pain Tolerant together require GM review rather than an assumed stacking rule. Disabled and duplicate traits, wounds, surprise, rolls, conditions, permissions, partial writes and concurrent clients need live verification. No Foundry session or automated tests were run.

observations.method: Compared the common and magical disease rules and selected disease stages on Core pages 116 and 120–121 with their stored embedded effects and the skill, defense and actor preparation paths; static inspection only.
observations.scope: Ataxia, Brain Rot, Rockjoint, common Black Heart Blight, Blood Lung, The Droops, Bone Break Fever, Frostlimb, Red Fever, Swamp Fever, Tunnel Cough, Yellow Tick, Witbane, The Rattles, Shakes, Chills, Collywobbles, Dampworm, Greenspore, Helljoint, Rust Chancre and the three stages of Ash Chancre, Chanthrax Blight, Ash Woe Blight, Black-Heart Blight, Astral Vapors, Lycanthropic Disease and Vampiric Disease. The source-only follow-up corrects the Ataxia, Rockjoint and common Black Heart Blight effects while retaining their IDs.
observations.limitations: Current Ataxia Items still apply the stored -10 to all Subterfuge tests. If an Intelligence-based roll includes that effect, the GM offsets the extra -10; do not offset Agility-based tests. After verified rebuild and reimport of the corrected source, apply -10 manually only to Agility-based Subterfuge. Current Rockjoint Items reduce Strength by 10 instead of Strength Bonus by 1; common Black Heart Blight uses fixed penalties instead of one added encumbrance level. The GM reviews those effects before correcting actor values and avoids counting both old and corrected penalties. Shared Diseased and Social Stigma effects, stage progression, cure, disease-specific missing clauses and Ash Chancre's third-stage Frenzied condition require manual review. Brain Rot's stored -15 maximum Magicka is not established by the source extract's wording 'Drain Magicka'; the GM must determine how the source handles the current and maximum pools. Existing actor Items and effects are not repaired. Verify active effects, toggles, chosen skill characteristic, duplicate stages, permissions, cure and partial or concurrent writes in Foundry. No Foundry session or automated tests were run.

observations.method: Compared Core birthsign power text, stored activation fields, ritual selection at rest, surprise-state handling and the shared roll and wound paths; static inspection only.
observations.scope: Mara's Gift, Blessed Touch, Blessed Word, Moonshadow, Treasure Seeker and Akaviri Danger-Sense. The latter now asks the operator to confirm a separately resolved optional Luck test instead of automatically rolling.
observations.limitations: The first five Items have disabled activation and their actual use, costs, choice, duration and daily tracking remain manual. The Ritual rest workflow can replace named blessing Items; inspect those Items and any partial replacement before retrying. The Akaviri dialog is an operator's record of the player's choice and manual result, not remote consent or a durable roll receipt. Closing it leaves the state unchanged; a changed combat or surprise state blocks the decision, and an unconfirmed write requires inspection before retry. The name-based lookup now uses the shared feature-enabled check. Verify source identity, enabled and disabled Items, repeated and declined tests, permissions, failed writes and concurrent clients in Foundry. No Foundry session or automated tests were run.

observations.method: Compared six Core power descriptions and stored activations with the generic activation, feature dispatch, form and outcome paths; static inspection only.
observations.scope: Vampiric Drain, Bat Form, Call of the Wolf, Thrill of the Chase, The Calling and Ancestor Guardian now use source-identified manual activation instructions before generic costs or uses. The source-only follow-up corrects Bat Form's action label and records Call of the Wolf's 1 AP cost.
observations.limitations: A recognized Item now requires the player and GM to resolve its complete procedure manually; it does not pay or consume a use through the guarded activation. Prior use, resources, damage, effects and actor forms are not repaired. Copies without a recognized source tag or exact compendium origin may bypass the guard. The source's once-per-day wording for Call of the Wolf is tracked manually rather than assumed to mean the stored Long Rest reset. Its Bestial Instinct rank and Bat Form state and expiry are manual. Verify source and origin matching, cancellation, permissions, choices, reflect, damage and healing, transformations, durations, manual use and costs, partial writes and concurrent clients in Foundry. No Foundry session or automated tests were run.

observations.method: Compared Core pages 206–207 and the named shout profiles on pages 210–213 with each saved activation and the generic activation and cost paths; static inspection only.
observations.scope: The one- and two-word Fleshrend, Frost Breath, Dismay, Slow Time and Unrelenting Force Items now use the existing source-identified manual guard. Disarm's prior manual guidance also specifies success and failure Stamina costs and recovery.
observations.limitations: The old generic activation spent 1 SP before the result, though a successful one-word shout has no word-based Stamina cost, and did not establish the full result or recovery. The guard charges no action, use or resource and requires manual declaration, Thu'um roll, success/failure costs, Voice talent exceptions, targets, effects and recovery. Prior charges and effects are not repaired. Copies without a recognized source tag or exact compendium origin may bypass the guard. Verify cancellation, known words, action and resource payment, failed/successful one- and two-word tests, Voice talents, targets, choices, duration, recovery, permissions, interrupted writes and concurrent use in Foundry. No Foundry session or automated tests were run.

observations.method: Compared the saved description and selected talent metadata with each available named Core feature extract; static field comparison only.
observations.scope: All 340 powers, talents and traits have an extract comparison: 334 match the selected extract fields and six lack an unambiguous named section.
observations.limitations: An extract can contain unrelated text or omit clauses. Matching text and metadata do not establish every passive contribution, activation, choice, cost, outcome, expiry or runtime path. Most features still have no selected execution trace, and even an existing selected trace is not a completed clause-by-clause review. Check each ledger entry against the source and workflow, and record specific unresolved clauses. No Foundry session or automated tests were run.

observations.method: Compared Core pages 88–89 and the current Item activation, usage and racial feature dispatch paths; static inspection only.
observations.scope: Ancestor's Wrath and Lord of the Hunt source-recognized manual activation guards.
observations.limitations: The recognized Core talent activation now gives instructions and exits before consuming an activation use or cost. Existing consumed uses and effects are not restored. Older untagged, copied or edited Items can bypass identification. Ancestor's Wrath still requires manual Sanctuary and Fire Cloak resolution; the source-only follow-up changes its action label and short text, pending native rebuild. Lord of the Hunt still requires manual terrain, test, Invisible expiry and use tracking. Verify compendium-origin and source-tag recognition, cost and rest tracking, cancellation, actor permissions, other racial talents and disabled automation in Foundry. No Foundry session or automated tests were run.

observations.method: Compared selected stored fields with recorded Core equipment tables and general descriptions; inspected selected preparation and damage-reduction paths. These field comparisons do not establish complete usage behavior. Static review only.
observations.scope: 1,141 of 1,192 Items have at least a qualified source-field comparison, including weapons, armor, ammunition, shields, gear, trade goods, potions, arcane Items and templates. The 51 remaining Items lack an exact source match. Sixteen misclassified Punch Daggers, 24 Magic-quality mismatches and two Werebear profiles are corrected in the source-only follow-up; 16 Cestus descriptions receive manual configuration instructions.
observations.limitations: The 3 unnamed arrow records use an explicit Iron assumption. Weapon values are base profiles; material and quality derivation, purchase handling, custom data and live use remain unverified. Cestus and Punch Dagger damage must be configured from the wielder's natural weapon. Current Adamantium and Stalhrim armor pieces retain incorrect Magic qualities until corrected and reimported; review them manually when fighting incorporeal opponents. Magic AR or BR no longer alone marks armor or shields as having the Magic quality; existing homebrew relying on that inference can change. Runed/charged behavior remains as before and requires review. Earlier damage and actor Items are not repaired. Check worn coverage, typed armor, shield blocks, cancellation, permissions, partial writes and concurrent clients in Foundry. No Foundry session or automated tests were run.

observations.method: Compared Core pages 84, 86, 89, 104 and 173, the affected authored Item identities, condition upsert, expertise matching, attack declaration and damage execution paths; static inspection only.
observations.scope: Numeric Bleeding and Burning creation, confirmed Bleeding reporting for From Oblivion's Heart, longest weapon-name matching, dual-capability expertise reminders, and Cestus/Punch Dagger source profiles and attack guards. Werebear bite and claw alternative-quality guard and source correction.
observations.limitations: No Foundry session or automated tests were run. Check first and repeated Bleeding and Burning, existing conditions, immunities, failed creation or updates, simultaneous clients and recovery. Earlier doubled conditions are not repaired. Verify prefixed Dai-Katana versus Katana, Great Flail versus Flail, and thrown-capable melee reminders and attacks. The source-only follow-up corrects 16 Punch Daggers but the current packs remain unchanged. For recognized Cestus and corrected Punch Dagger Items, enter the wielder's base natural-weapon damage before attacking; Eye of Night may already increase the die and Pugilist remains manual. Existing misclassified Punch Daggers must be reimported after a verified rebuild or resolved manually. Older untagged or edited Items and already committed cards may bypass an early guard. Confirm owner and GM permissions, cancellation, failed writes and repeated actions. Current Werebear Bite and Claw Items contain both qualities despite enabled=false; select exactly one in the Item sheet. The source-only follow-up keeps one default until the player chooses another.

observations.method: Compared the recorded Core pages 81 and 85–87 with the current damage, opposed attack, shield-block and feature-outcome paths; static inspection only.
observations.scope: Manual choice safeguards for Hammerblow, Death by a Thousand Cuts, Red Legion Throw and The Whirling School; target-size gating for Monster Hunter; removal of Pugilist's unconditional damage bonus, unsafe Bruiser, Dart Thrower, Sneak Attack and Assassinate damage components, and Bruiser's unconfirmed mace Stamina update; manual next-test tracking for new Inspire Heroism uses; and declaration reminders for other traced weapon-expertise clauses. Precise, Eye of Night and Viper's Eye penalty-offset stacking; Blademaster and Viper's Eye manual reminders.
observations.limitations: Verify normal, failed, zero-damage and blocked attacks; optional choices and cancellations; Large, Huge, Enormous, smaller and missing sizes; disabled talents and multiple threshold modifiers. Check the declaration reminder as the weapon changes and confirm it does not lead to duplicated ordinary weapon-quality or TN effects. Attack-card reminders require a declared weapon that can be resolved; otherwise consult the talent description. Check GM and owner permissions, stale cards, pending Inspired outcomes, existing Inspired effects, failed chat or usage writes, and concurrent clients. Existing conditions, resource changes and Inspired effects are not reversed. Inspect prior costs and outcomes before retrying. Manual procedures are not live-verified. Check Precision Strike previews and committed rolls with each talent alone and together; the quality and reach changes remain manual.

observations.method: Compared Core pages 19 and 133 with the existing Power Draw effect, reload shortcut, AP spending and combat-step helpers; static checks only.
observations.scope: Nonconsuming Power Draw guard and ordinary reload payment, weapon-state, combat-step and chat-report safeguards.
observations.limitations: Power Draw and the first Reload reduction of a conjured weapon remain GM-resolved. Verify a pending effect and stored reduction, selection cancellation, a benefit appearing while a dialog is open, insufficient AP, free and multi-step reloads, combat-step and equipment changes, permissions, payment or Item failures and missing chat. Older partial reloads may already have lost a reduction. A local commit lock does not serialize clients, and separate writes have no durable recovery hold; inspect AP, effect, weapon and chat before retrying. No Foundry session or automated tests were run.

observations.method: Compared Core pages 108, 142–144 and 253 with the three touch-spell records, the legacy restoration classifier, condition, wound, death-test and managed-healing paths; static checks only.
observations.scope: Recognized Core Stabilize and Cure Paralysis manual guidance, Healing Touch's selected healing path, and rejection of unrelated legacy operation kinds by resource restoration.
observations.limitations: The recognized Stabilize spell now warns rather than running first aid on the current targets. Confirm one dying character within one meter and manage death tests manually; the existing stabilization marker is coupled to first aid and does not distinguish wound penalties. Existing first-aid markers are not changed. Cure Paralysis remains manual; check the condition source and one-meter range. Healing Touch's configured flag routes normal casts to a healing outcome, but exactly one target and range need GM confirmation. Exercise all Healing Touch levels, full and wounded targets, failed and cancelled casts, altered or unrecognized Items, permissions, repeated actions, pending cards, partial writes and concurrent clients. Confirm Fortify, Resistance, disease cures and other unrelated legacy operations do not restore HP, while configured resource restoration and healing still work. Previous outcomes are not reversed. No Foundry session or automated tests were run.

observations.method: Compared Core page 143 and the alchemy effect on page 253 with all seven Replenish levels, the restoration configuration and direct casting, serialized potion and managed-outcome paths; static checks only.
observations.scope: Pending application and the configured Spell Strength/Casting Cost cap for source-recognized Core Replenish.
observations.limitations: Check levels 1–7, missing and full target MP, actual casting spend and cost reductions, distinct target and caster, serialized spell potions at multiple levels, selected and changed targets, cancellations, permissions, old cards, duplicate clicks and interrupted or concurrent applications. The implementation uses the recorded casting spend as Casting Cost; its interaction with reductions needs source and live confirmation. Enchanted Items and no-Magicka casts require GM resolution. The GM must confirm the one-meter range. For source-recognized Rejuvenate and Replenish scrolls, verify cancellation, rejected or partial casts, successful and failed rolls, quantity and uncertain consumption; the generic scroll path needs separate review. Older unrecognized or altered Items and previously resolved cards without an outcome need review before any paid cost is repeated. No Foundry session or automated tests were run.

observations.method: Compared the Combat Style rule on Core page 69 with Item preparation, combat attack TNs and opposed skill declarations; static checks only.
observations.scope: Agility for ranged attacks and the declared characteristic in skill-opposed Combat Style lanes, for eligible owned Combat Style Items; selected-characteristic adjustments in the shared skill TN are now counted once.
observations.limitations: Check different Strength and Agility totals, both base characteristics, melee and ranged previews and committed rolls, skill-opposed attacker and defender selections, wound and fatigue, Active Effects, unusual-combat caps, equipment, permissions and changed data. Verify other skills with different selected/base characteristics: their TNs can change because the earlier calculation counted the difference twice. A missing or incorrect attack mode, missing totals, other base characteristics and NPC profession fallback remain manual. Character choice in the ordinary melee/defense dialogs and characteristic-specific combat modifiers still need separate review. No Foundry session or automated tests were run.

observations.method: Compared Core pages 78, 154-155 and 160 with the existing creation, potion and minor-effect tables and the brew and drink paths; static checks only.
observations.scope: Source-correct table descriptions and manual handling of creation backfires and backfired potions.
observations.limitations: Potion and toxin creation backfire outcomes now record a 1d4 result and stop for GM resolution before ingredient, Item or Trial and Error changes; a potential poison backfire waits for a GM decision without a table roll. Potion consumption backfires are blocked before costs for manual resolution. Existing items and outcomes produced with the former tables are not corrected. Some old serialized outcomes do not carry enough information to recognize a backfire. Verify all table results and dice, normal brews and potions, GM instructions, permissions, concurrent clients, cancellation, lost acknowledgements and interrupted claims. The brew claim and separate card, roll, ingredient and Item writes are not a cross-client transaction. The exported roll helpers report entries; they do not resolve consequences. No Foundry session or automated tests were run.

observations.method: Compared the Core spell, potion and alchemy effect on pages 143, 185 and 253 with authoring configuration and the shared casting, potion and managed-outcome paths; static checks only.
observations.scope: Explicit Stamina-or-Fatigue selection for the identified Core Rejuvenate spell and catalog potion effect, including source-recognized serialized potion spells.
observations.limitations: The earlier potion scenario used the old automatic Fatigue-first choice and is not evidence for this change. Exercise normal and deferred casts, catalog and serialized potions, both choices with and without Fatigue or missing Stamina, cancellation before costs, changed recipient state, old pending cards, backfire, permissions, repeated clicks and interrupted or concurrent operations. The GM must confirm the spell's one-meter range; the current range selector does not recognize touch and other casting paths need review. Reflected casts, changed restoration settings and older copies without provenance require GM review. The choice dialog does not obtain remote consent. The selected and compiled spell metadata still asserts Fatigue-first; revision 20261030-6 corrects it but needs a native rebuild. No Foundry session or automated tests were run.

observations.method: Book pages 88-89, the Core Argonian, Bosmer and Nord grants and shared feature and resistance paths inspected; static checks only.
observations.scope: Child of the Sap, Nature's Blessing and Sons of Skyrim passive prerequisites and duplicate/manual-field handling.
observations.limitations: Verify standard racial traits, absent and disabled traits, duplicate talents and traits, explicit numeric talent fields, manually adjusted trait and unrelated bonuses, disease immunity and checks, poison and frost resistance tests, damage, Speed, Wound Threshold and optional wounds. Automatic racial increases are conservatively gated; existing Actor totals may change, while ambiguous or separately hand-adjusted cases require GM review. The original Disease Resistance Item is not removed. No Foundry session or automated tests were run.

observations.method: Book pages 92-93, the existing racial trait representations, feature contributions and shared resistance selector inspected; static checks only.
observations.scope: Structured and legacy resistance trait selection and selected racial and Malacath's Fury upgrades.
observations.limitations: Verify PC and NPC characteristic, skill and opposed dialogs, base and duplicate structured or legacy traits, disabled features, Nature's Blessing, Sons of Skyrim, High Men, Lionheart and active/expired Malacath's Fury; compare selected test modifiers with damage resistance. The selector excludes equipment fields and does not treat percentage Disease Resistance as Resistance (Disease, X). Other Active Effect and manually configured sources need review, as do actor/effect changes while a dialog is open: the selected value is a snapshot. Check manually when resistance applies. No Foundry session or automated tests were run.

observations.method: Book pages 88 and 93, the Core Breton and Altmer grants and shared actor preparation and resistance paths inspected; static checks only.
observations.scope: Lionheart and Blood of Aldmeris standard additional Power Well and resistance upgrades.
observations.limitations: Verify standard and structured trait representations, separate and duplicate Power Wells, absent or disabled traits and talents, edited values, explicit talent fields, other manual bonuses, disease checks, magic resistance-test selection and existing Actors. Only single recognized unmodified racial bases are automatically upgraded; other cases need GM review. Existing Magicka and resistance totals may change and unrelated manual bonuses may overlap. No Foundry session or automated tests were run.

observations.method: Book page 90, the Core Redguard grants, derived trait profile and selected damage and disease-check paths inspected; static checks only.
observations.scope: High Men disease immunity and conservative poison-resistance upgrade.
observations.limitations: Verify disease immunity in the existing damage and disease-check paths, standard poison resistance, non-damaging resistance tests, feature enablement, missing and disabled traits, duplicate Items, edited values, explicit talent bonus fields and other manual adjustments. Only a single recognized standard poison trait is automatically increased. Existing Actor derived resistance can change, and unrelated manual bonuses may overlap. No Foundry session or automated tests were run.

observations.method: Book pages 89-90, the Core Orsimer race grants and shared trait/feature aggregation paths inspected; static checks only.
observations.scope: Wrothgarian Tough and Resilient upgrades and Malacath's Fury Resilient prerequisite.
observations.limitations: Verify one standard Resilient (3) and Tough (1), each feature independently and together, missing and disabled prerequisites, other names, trait and talent duplicates, explicitly configured talent fields, previously hand-adjusted actor or trait bonuses, optional wounds and feature enablement. The new contributor applies only to unambiguous recognized base values and does not identify all manual adjustments in unrelated fields. Malacath's automatic HP is no longer unconditional. Existing Actors' derived HP or Wound Threshold may change; inspect totals before play. No Foundry session or automated tests were run.

observations.method: Book pages 88-90 and the existing actor preparation, activation, outcome and rest paths inspected; static checks only.
observations.scope: Histskin and Malacath's Fury usage recording, healing and timed outcomes; Wrothgarian passive source trace.
observations.limitations: Verify separate Item-use and Actor-usage writes, already-used preflight, denied and interrupted writes, local and concurrent clients, short and long rests, cancellation, outcome order and expiry. A recorded use is retained if an outcome fails; inspect the Actor, Item and chat before retrying. New Malacath's Fury outcomes modify Strength Bonus rather than the Strength score; previously queued cards and existing effects retain the older change. The staged Free Action labels need the native pack rebuild. A separate observation covers Wrothgarian's new, conservatively gated passive contributor and existing manual adjustments. No Foundry session or automated tests were run.

observations.method: Book page 114, Horror outcomes, fear effects and their combat-boundary paths inspected; static checks only.
observations.scope: Vomiting and Hopeless delayed losses, Hopeless 1d6 duration, Blackout and survived Scared to Death 1d4-hour duration, and selected failure reports.
observations.limitations: Verify table boundaries, duration values and result summaries, permissions, effect creation failures, Scared to Death roll and death-state write failures, missing summary, retries and concurrent clients. Vomiting and Hopeless no longer deduct SP immediately; the GM checks the duration and applies the later loss and Fatigue manually. The existing next-turn/fixed-round effect expiry needs separate timing review. Blackout's rolled hours are recorded, but the GM tracks elapsed time and removes the effect. Existing older effects are not migrated. Momentary Blackout's unconsciousness and subsequent encounter penalty, Manic Terror's forced attack and subsequent SP loss, and Mind Break's duration, permanent loss and later restrictions need complete execution review. A result has no cross-client durable receipt; inspect chat and the actor before repeating anything. No Foundry session or automated tests were run.

observations.method: Book pages 19, 88, 94 and 111, activation costs, actor preparation and the selected magic application paths inspected; static checks only.
observations.scope: Dragonskin source-to-workflow trace and temporary-Stamina-first generic feature costs.
observations.limitations: Verify a temporary-only, regular-only and mixed cost, insufficient resources, cancellation, permissions, interrupted writes and simultaneous clients. Feature activation still blocks Stamina overdraw for GM resolution. The actor preparation pipeline clamps negative Stamina before deriving Fatigue; review existing actors, Stamina spend and loss, fatigue controls, rest and restoration together before changing that behavior. Dragonskin's staged Free Action label requires the native pack rebuild. Selected damage and healing use its absorption effect; effect-only magic does not enter that check, combat typed damage uses a separate trait-only path, and Reflect ordering and effect expiry need review. Verify behavior in Foundry. No Foundry session or automated tests were run.

observations.method: Berserker, Controlled Anger, Rage-fueled Frenzy and 'Tis But a Scratch source and Frenzied condition paths inspected; static checks only.
observations.scope: Feature-aware Frenzied talent lookup, effect-identified temporary-SP grants, bounded end loss, unconfirmed writes and removal, and manual temporary-Stamina reconciliation. Recognized Berserker and Controlled Anger activation now stop before generic payment or use and provide manual instructions.
observations.limitations: Verify enabled and disabled Controlled Anger, Berserker, Tis But a Scratch and Rage-fueled Frenzy, plus punctuation aliases. Test newly applied and pre-existing disabled effects, failed or repeated creation and grant, duplicate effects, talent toggles during an existing effect, voluntary and involuntary Frenzy, zero and low Stamina, mixed temporary and regular SP, the recorded paid and manual-review amounts, non-lethal limits, automatic and manual removal, duplicate hooks, failed deletion followed by a later-round retry, re-enabling the same effect with and without an unresolved earlier loss, older round-only end records, owner/GM permissions, failed or interrupted writes, and simultaneous clients. An unavailable portion of the loss is not applied automatically; the GM reviews Fatigue and the non-lethal limit without repeating the paid portion before re-enabling. New grants and end records are tied to the effect ID; the local lock and records are not cross-client transactions. The once-per-rest Free Action and involuntary control test remain manual. Temporary Stamina is not source-attributed; remaining temporary SP need GM review. No Foundry session or automated tests were run.

observations.method: Book pages 174 and 181, authored Items and their shared inventory and Snare code paths inspected; static checks only.
observations.scope: Bola, Rations, Cooking (Travel) Tools, Quiver, both Backpacks and Sack (30 ENC).
observations.limitations: Past selected Rations, Quiver, Snare and Bash scenarios predate later changes. Recheck current Foundry behavior, fractional ENC, quantity edits, invalid and nested containment, cycles, capacity, permissions, save failures, simultaneous clients and Snare boundaries. The GM decides physical fit, tool applicability, sack hand use and the source-undefined Snare maximum. The current quiver permits ammunition generally rather than distinguishing arrows and bolts. No Foundry session or automated tests were run for these traces.

observations.method: Book pages 98, 113 and 114, the current fear paths and combat-boundary payload inspected; static checks only.
observations.scope: Panic effect confirmation and duration, non-combat concentration penalty, Lost Composure reaction restrictions, manual flight and Snap Out timing.
observations.limitations: Verify initial and table-roll message failures, interruption after the table roll, Panic effect and summary failures, new and older Lost Composure and Frightened effects, Startled, non-combat fear near and away from the source, and unrelated tests. The GM handles concentration eligibility, Running and Screaming flight and its Snap Out eligibility; older effects may retain previous flags or a broad penalty. The boundary reads prior/current turn data and offers an optional Snap Out roll. A recorded success waits until its turn ends; interrupted or stale settlements leave a GM review hold. Check cancellation, shared test modifiers, failed rolls, first-turn and initiative changes, rewinds, GM loss, combat ending, missing effects, all writes, recovery and concurrent clients. observations.observed: A recorded successful casting result and creature Willpower roll produced a bound Daedra; its synthetic Actor received Summoned, Bound and restrained effects, and the caster received Strength-2 Mindlock linked to the origin. A summon without a recorded casting result stayed pending; the GM recorded an unbound result without creating Bound, Mindlock or a restraint penalty.
observations.limitations: Initiative and unbound end-of-round persistence are manual. Ghost and Wraith binding use a separate rule and remain manual. This observation predates the current binding, ownership and recovery changes; the new implementation requires live verification.

observations.method: Manual inspection of synthetic token Actors, combat tracker and regeneration outcome in Foundry 14.369.
observations.observed: The controlled Daedra received Regeneration 6 from its caster’s WB and appeared in round-start prompts; the unbound Daedra received 0 and no prompt. An Endurance failure healed nothing; a later success and Apply Outcome healed the controlled Daedra from 5 to 11 HP.
observations.limitations: Talent removal, changing caster WB, different creature traits, and multi-client behavior still require live verification.

observations.method: Manual character-sheet activations, authoritative Apply Outcome controls, native state inspection and world-time advance.
observations.observed: One activation spent 1 SP and gave each of two summoned Daedra +6 Natural Toughness. Both effects expired after 7 seconds in the configured 6-second round. Two subsequent applications to one Daedra produced one effect and +6, and activation at 0 SP was refused. A new application refreshed the existing effect start from one initiative step to the next. A summon outside the combat tracker received a one-round effect; it remained through the matching turn in the next round and was removed at that turn’s end.
observations.limitations: This observation predates the revised expiry implementation. Combat deletion, initiative changes, delayed outcomes across combat transitions, cross-scene and multi-client cases, permissions, and partial-failure recovery remain unverified on the current build.

observations.method: Manual placement cancellation through the spell outcome and native cancellation of a disposable origin in Foundry 14.369.
observations.observed: Cancelling placement created no creature and produced a review status with an explanation that the paid casting cost and origin remain. The final implementation produced no cancellation error in the console. Ending a separate bound fixture origin removed its linked token while another unbound fixture from a different origin remained.
observations.limitations: This observation predates the revised cleanup implementation. Mixed bound and unbound summons sharing one origin, player permissions, concurrent cancellation, and recovery after a failed linked deletion remain unverified on the current build.

observations.method: Manual native Item import, character-sheet interaction and advancement-service purchase in Foundry 14.369.
observations.observed: Rite of Conjuring was classified as a ritual costing 25 XP. Its normal spell-cast attempt was blocked with manual instructions. The Magic tab grouped it under Rituals and opened its description; the Item header showed Ritual and See description. A separate disposable character purchased one copy for 25 XP, moving from 900 to 875.
observations.limitations: The individual ritual procedures, components, tests and consequences remain manual. Other rites, non-GM purchase permissions, configured payment modes, and NPC sheet presentation require live verification.

observations.method: Manual invocation of the Chapter 4 and Chapter 6 diagnostic APIs in isolated Foundry 14.369.
observations.observed: The diagnostics returned four traced Chapter 4 items and two traced Chapter 6 items, with eight clauses in total. An untraced entry reported no trace, and catalog statuses were labeled as static hints rather than execution proof.
observations.limitations: Only the selected clauses are traced; all other clauses remain unreviewed.

observations.method: Manual sheet actions and opposed-roll choices in disposable Foundry 14.369 world.
observations.observed: At 2 meters, selecting the equipped Bola for Trip offered only the attacker’s Combat Style and the defender’s Athletics or Evade. A successful opposed result applied Prone. At 5 meters, selecting Bola for Bash created the opposed action card. After the token-selection fix and reload, a new Trip card still identified the intended attacker and defender while an unrelated token was controlled. This initial sheet scenario did not cover normal unarmed actions, Special Advantage, Bash outcomes, range boundaries, target size, combat AP, cancellation, permissions or stale cards; see the later selected observations. The later shared Snare workflow prompts for a GM decision when distance exceeds the listed range or cannot be measured; the rule itself does not specify a maximum.

observations.method: Manual use of native review macros, Foundry dialogs, and persisted outcome controls in an isolated 14.369 world. The source combat result was a disposable recorded fixture, not a full attack.
observations.observed: A free Special Advantage created an opposed Snare Trip card with the attacker limited to Combat Style and the defender limited to Athletics or Evade. A separate legacy Trip card displayed those choices and offered only Athletics or Evade in the defender dialog. A legacy card refused to roll after the Bola was unequipped. An existing Special Advantage child card refused a roll when the defender became larger. In a separate recorded-result fixture during active combat, Snare Trip auto-win applied Prone and the attacker’s AP decreased from 3 to 2. At 0 AP, auto-win produced no Trip effect; after correction, its card says No effect applied and its saved action result reports blocked. An actual full attack-to-advantage flow, duplicate submissions, permission failures, and multiple clients remain unverified.

observations.method: Manual legacy-action review using placed tokens in an isolated Foundry 14.369 world.
observations.observed: At 18 scene units, a Bola with 15 listed long range displayed the explicit GM decision; cancellation stopped the action and approval created an opposed card. A larger target was rejected. Exact range boundaries, non-meter scenes, concurrent changes while dialogs are open and player/GM permissions remain unverified.

observations.method: Manual application of standalone Bash outcomes in the isolated world, with and without a disposable active combat.
observations.observed: Outside tracked combat the result reported no AP deduction and a failed Acrobatics roll with manual knockback. In tracked combat the defender moved from 2 AP to 1; a subsequent Bash at 0 AP reported that none was available. Both in-combat examples rolled Acrobatics and reported the failed result. Acrobatics success, permission failure, interrupted stages, repeat application and attacker AP costs remain unverified.
